message.content:
**Short answer:** Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s not the city council that handles it directly. Noise complaints are usually taken by the **Atlanta Police Department (APD)** or the city’s **Code‑Enforcement/Code‑Compliance** office. The city council may review the complaint later, but the first stop is the police or the 311 service. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Step | What to Do | Where / How | |------|------------|-------------| | 1 | **Call 311** (non‑emergency) | 404‑656‑3111 (or dial 311 from any Atlanta phone) | | 2 | **Use the online portal** | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 – you can submit a “Noise” request and attach photos or a video if you have one. | | 3 | **Contact APD directly** | 404‑656‑3111 (same number as 311) – they’ll dispatch an officer or a code‑enforcement officer to investigate. | | 4 | **File a formal complaint** | If the issue persists, you can file a written complaint with the **City of Atlanta Code‑Enforcement Office**. Mail or email it to:
City of Atlanta
Department of Public Safety – Code Enforcement
200 West Peachtree Street, Suite 400
Atlanta, GA 30303 | | 5 | **Follow up** | Keep the reference number you receive from 311 or APD. You can check status online or call 311 again. | ### Quick links | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | 311 online portal | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 | | Noise ordinance (what’s prohibited) | https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/department-of-public-safety/department-of-public-safety-division-of-traffic-and-transportation/traffic-ordinances/noise-ordinance | | City of Atlanta Police Department | https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/department-of-public-safety/department-of-public-safety-division-of-traffic-and-transportation | | City of Atlanta Code‑Enforcement | https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/department-of-public-safety/department-of-public-safety-division-of-traffic-and-transportation | --- ## What the Noise Ordinance Covers - **Quiet hours:** 10 p.m. – 6 a.m. (most residential areas). - **Allowed activities:** lawn mowing, power washing, etc., are generally permitted during daytime hours. - **Penalties:** Repeated violations can lead to fines, citations, or even civil action. If you’re dealing with a **persistent or severe** noise issue (e.g., a neighbor’s loud party, construction, or a commercial operation that’s violating the ordinance), the APD will typically issue a citation and may refer the matter to the city council’s **Public Safety Committee** for further action. --- ## Tips for a Successful Complaint 1. **Document the noise** – record the time, duration, and type of sound. 2. **Provide evidence** – photos, videos, or audio clips help the officer assess the situation. 3. **Be specific** – mention the address, the source (e.g., a party, construction site), and any relevant details. 4. **Stay polite** – a calm tone often speeds up the response. 5. **Keep records** – note the reference number, date, and any follow‑up actions. --- ### Bottom line - **Yes, you can report noise complaints in Atlanta.** - **Use 311 or the APD’s online portal** for the quickest response. - **The city council itself isn’t the first point of contact**, but they’ll review the case if it escalates. If you need more detailed guidance on the ordinance or want to know how to appeal a citation, let me know!
